To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a phenol extraction of Streptococcus pyogenes M serotype 3 (GCSY3) vaccine resulted in the production of a vaccine that elicited higher titres than did heat-killing of GCSY3, and that the phenol-extracted vaccine elicited antibodies with reduced cross-reactivity to Streptococcus equisimilis M serotype 1.
phenol extraction of Streptococcus pyogenes cells increases the specificity of M-typing fluorescent antibodies.
the use of phenol extraction for preparation of vaccines against the M-serotype of group A Stretpococcus results in antisera of higher titer and reduced cross-reactivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a vaccine for group A streptocsocci.
the use of fluorescent antibody staining to detect the presence of group A strep in throat cultures.

the development of a vaccine to protect against streptococcal infections, especially those caused by group A streptoccus, and with the development of an immunofluoresence method to identify the M-serotypes of the group A streptoccoci.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of phenol-extracted vaccine in the preparation of fluorescent typing sera is recommended.
phenol extraction of streptococci is an efficient method for the preparation of vaccines and antisera for M-typing of group A Strepto- coccus.

the use of phenol-extracted vaccine in the preparation of conjugates for M typing by immunofluorecence has the following advantages: (a) higher titers are obtained; (b) specificity is increased; and (c) the conjugates may be used at a lower concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phenol extraction of the bacteria prior to immunization is a better procedure than the conventional heating method for the production of antisera for fluorescent typing of group A strepto-cocci.

immunization of rabbits with heat-killed cells of the three M serotypes, M-1, M-3, and M-12, resulted in production of sera which were reactive with the homologous serotype and which did not show crossreactivity with other M serotypes.
phenol extracted cells of streptococcus are more immunogenic than heat-killed cells for eliciting antisera for M-serotype specific fluorescent typing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of phenol-extracted vaccine may be advantageous over conventional heat-killed vaccine for the production of immunofluorescein conjugates for the rapid screening of group A strep strains for M-serotypes.

phenol extraction of Streptococcus pyogenes can improve the specificity of fluorescent M-serotyping antisera, and that this technique may be used to improve the quality of serotyping antisera for other bacterial species.

we have demonstrated the potential of using a combination of phenol-extraction, heat inactivation, and fluorescent antibody staining as a rapid method for screening for M-serotype in clinical samples.
